title: Nell's Noisy Hive
checkpoint: Phase 1 (Introduction) — instrumental sounds and body percussion. Read this one ALOUD to the children.
note_for_grown_ups: An Introduction-phase book — no decoding, you read it aloud. Every page has a sound to make with your hands, feet or a simple instrument. Do the sound TWICE: once loud, once as quietly as you possibly can.

pages.text: Nell was making a band. A band needs sounds, and Nell had none at all yet.
pages.join_in: Rub your palms together. That is the very quietest sound you can make.
pages.illustration: Nell the sunflower-yellow bumblebee hovering in front of a tidy hive behind tall sunflowers, holding an empty jam jar like a conductor holding nothing. Bright, busy, comic. Her tuft of fluff sticks up with effort.

pages.text: She found two sticks. Tap, tap, tap. That was one sound.
pages.join_in: Tap two fingers together — tap, tap, tap.
pages.illustration: Two dry twigs held in Nell's front legs, striking together. Draw the moment of contact with a tiny puff of dust. Sunflower stems make warm vertical stripes behind her.

pages.text: She found an old tin. Boom! That was much too loud, so she tried again gently. Boom.
pages.join_in: Pat your knees — first BIG, then tiny.
pages.illustration: A dented tin can lying on its side; Nell drumming the base with both front legs. Show the first BOOM with the tin tipping over and a startled ladybird flying off it. Playful chaos.

pages.text: Ned came to help. He slapped the pond with one flat foot. Splat! The water jumped.
pages.join_in: Slap your hands on your legs — splat!
pages.illustration: Ned the gold duckling at the reedy pond edge, one webbed foot down flat, a wide flat splash ring spreading out. Water droplets caught in the air. Ned looks extremely pleased with himself.

pages.text: Then Nell stamped. Then she clapped. Then she did both, one after the other, faster and faster.
pages.join_in: Stamp, clap. Stamp, clap. Now speed up!
pages.illustration: Nell mid-air with all six legs in different positions, a blur of movement lines. Ned watching with his beak open. Keep the composition diagonal so it feels fast.

pages.text: At the end Nell held up one leg and everybody stopped. The garden went completely quiet.
pages.join_in: Hold up one finger. Now — nobody make a sound. Count to three.
pages.illustration: Nell frozen with one leg raised like a conductor's baton, everyone else caught mid-stop: Ned's foot half lifted, the tin still rocking. Very still composition, lots of white space, the opposite of the previous page.

pages.text: "That," said Nell, "is the best sound of all."
pages.join_in: Listen to the quiet with your eyes shut. What can you hear inside it?
pages.illustration: Simple, calm final page. Nell sitting on the upturned tin at dusk with Ned beside her, both looking out at the darkening garden. Warm low light. No movement lines anywhere.
